title: PxCorpus: A Spoken Drug Prescription Dataset in French
why_promising: Primary non-singing French production collected experimentally from 55 participants (doctors, other medical experts, and non-experts), with roughly four hours of speech and 2067 recordings reported. Zenodo states that automatic transcriptions were verified by human effort and that the recordings are manually transcribed and semantically annotated. The deposit exposes synchronized recording paths, participant metadata, transcripts, intent/entity labels, dialogue events, and manual dialogue-quality annotations under CC BY 4.0. This is potentially useful for speech-production metadata, disfluencies, timing at recording/session level, demographic/group comparisons, and future acoustic extraction from primary recordings.
open_question: Keep in review until file-level inspection determines whether any phone/segment/prosodic boundaries or production measurements were manually created or exhaustively human-verified. If not, retain as a discovery/review source rather than promoting semantic/transcription-only annotations to the phonetic core. Enumerate PxCorpus.zip contents, preserve paths/metadata/seq files source-faithfully, and avoid treating ASR event text or system TTS as human phonetic annotation.
